> 天下有始，以為天下母。既得其母，以知其子；既知其子，復守其母.

Chapter 51 was about how the source nourishes. Chapter 52 is about how a person returns to it.

The road back is drawn as a closed loop: from mother to child is going out; from child to mother is coming back.

And on that road, four characters mean something entirely different from what they mean today.

## 兌 is a mouth

In the 易 configuration, 兌 is the mouth. So 塞其兌 is to stop up the mouth — the place where things come out and where things are taken in.

## 勤 is toil

勤: 勞也 — labor, exertion. 終身不勤 is not "never diligent"; it is never having to labor.

## 救 is to stop

救: 止也 — to stop, to halt. 終身不救 is not "beyond saving" as a verdict; it is never being able to stop.

That reversal matters. The usual reading of 終身不救 is a threat — you will be lost forever. Read correctly, it is a description: the one who keeps opening the aperture will spend a lifetime unable to halt.

## 襲 is a layered robe

襲: 左衽袍也 — a robe worn with the lapel crossing left, worn in layers.

So 是謂襲常 is: this is called wearing the 常 like a garment — layer over layer, put on every day.

## 既得其母，以知其子

Having got the mother, you know the child. The child is everything that has come into being — the world as it presents itself.

> 既知其子，復守其母，沒身不殆.

Having known the child, return and keep the mother. To the end of life, without peril.

The order is the whole point. The chapter does not despise the child — it fully acknowledges that you must know the world. The instruction comes after: knowing it, go back and hold the source.

復 is the hinge: it is the return, and it is voluntary. Nothing about knowing the child sends you back automatically.

## 見小曰明，守柔曰強

Seeing the small is called 明; holding softness is called 強.

小 is not "trivial." It is what has not yet become visible: the beginning of a movement, the first sign. Seeing it is the same 明 as chapters 16, 33, and 45 — the clarity that comes from reading the pattern before the event.

守柔 as 強 is chapter 43's 柔 again, and the same claim: the position that can bend does not need to be defended.

## 用其光，復歸其明

Use its light, and return to its 明.

光 is the beam — what you can direct: attention, analysis, the spotlight you aim at things.

明 is the illumination that is not yours to aim.

So the instruction is a loop: use the beam, and come back to the source of the light. Not "stop using the beam" — use it, and return.

Which is the most practical line in the chapter, because it names the failure precisely: using the light so continuously that you forget it has a source, and then treating your beam as the standard.

## 無遺身殃

Leave no calamity to the body.

The chapter closes on the body, as chapter 50 did. Both are saying the same thing: the cost of not returning is paid physically, not abstractly.
